extracted.intended_audience: users of Mathematics Stack Exchange (askers and answerers), especially new or inexperienced participants
extracted.subtask_description: Community FAQ and guidelines for participating on Mathematics Stack Exchange: how to format math, choose tags, handle homework, respond to and improve questions, when to refer to other sites, and basic etiquette for askers and answerers.

rubrics_metrics.name: How do I type math in my question/answer/comment?
rubrics_metrics.description: You can use TeX markup. To type inline TeX equations, surround the code with $'s. To put the equation in its own line, surround with $$'s. AMS math environments are also supported.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples are given (inline: $c = \sqrt{ a^2 + b^2 - 2ab \cos \theta }$, display: $$\int_0^\infty e^{-x^2} dx = \frac{\sqrt\pi}2$$). If unfamiliar with TeX, find a question that uses the markup you want and view source. Links to MathJax and additional resources are provided. For detailed TeX/LaTeX questions, this is not the appropriate place — use tex.stackexchange.com or latex-community.org.

rubrics_metrics.name: Math rendering / dollar-signs troubleshooting
rubrics_metrics.description: The things in between dollar signs are math formulas written using TeX markup and should be converted by MathJax.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If formulas don't render in a preview, wait ~4 seconds for automatic rendering. If rendering fails in refreshed comments, that's known behavior. If neither applies, refresh the browser, ensure JavaScript is enabled (including for mathjax.org), and consider disabling browser extensions/custom scripts (e.g., NoScript).

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate forum: Math.StackExchange vs MathOverflow
rubrics_metrics.description: MathOverflow is designed for professional mathematicians asking and answering research-level questions; Math.SE is intended for enthusiasts and users of mathematics to ask and answer questions about mathematics in general.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The cultures differ; exceptionally difficult or research-oriented questions may be referred to MathOverflow. If a question is graduate-level or has professional research interest, consider MO. See linked pages about differences and referrals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other websites/resources to consult
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommended external resources for various needs: Wolfram Alpha (direct calculations/calculus), Dr. Math (elementary to middle-undergraduate), Art of Problem Solving (high-school / contest / some undergraduate), StackOverflow (programming/implementation), Cross Validated (statistics/probability), Theoretical Computer Science (research-level TCS).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the site most appropriate to the problem type; no website substitutes for in-person help — consult teachers, professors, or TAs as appropriate. Links to curated lists of resources are provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper way to respond to homework questions (answering homework)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a question appears to be homework and lacks previous work, request a revision showing effort. Give the asker a chance to respond before voting to close.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid giving a complete solution that can be copied verbatim — this discourages learning and turns the site into a free homework service. Prefer hints to point the student in the right direction. It is encouraged to suggest parallel problems that use the same principles. You may later edit your answer to be more complete after a suitable amount of time (or if the asker posts their own correct answer). Be polite and encouraging; do not ridicule students. While don't automatically downvote someone for posting a full answer in good faith, feel free to downvote overly complete answers to known homework if appropriate. Related meta discussions and links are provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling homework questions (askers' expectations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Askers of homework-like questions are expected to show previous work and thought.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the question lacks previous work, answerers may request an edit. Read the FAQ sections on 'How to ask a homework question' and general 'How to ask a good question' for details; failure to show effort can lead to closure or downvotes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Why was my question closed?
rubrics_metrics.description: A short reason for closure will typically be given in the comments. Being closed doesn't necessarily mean your question is bad; it often means it's not appropriate for Math.SE in its present form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Math.SE prefers questions that are specific, mathematical, and have an answerable form. Homework-style questions should show effort. Read the 'How to ask a good question' and 'How to ask a homework question' guidance. If you believe closure was mistaken after reading the FAQ, ask about it on meta.

rubrics_metrics.name: Must I post in English?
rubrics_metrics.description: Post in the language you are most comfortable with.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Often someone will translate your question to English. Many users prefer a clear question that can be translated over an unclear question written in English as a second language.

rubrics_metrics.name: What do I do if I don't get an answer after several days?
rubrics_metrics.description: Wait longer for advanced or niche topics, as answerers may not yet have seen it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You can set a bounty (spend reputation) to attract attention. Check that your question is tagged properly — avoid overly-specific tags that reduce visibility. If the question is particularly advanced (graduate level or higher), consider whether it belongs on MathOverflow. Links explain how to set a bounty and tag decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: What tags should I use for my question?
rubrics_metrics.description: Tagging guidance: use (but not abuse) meta-tags (e.g., big-list, reference-request, soft-question); indicate the branch of mathematics; tag with the related external field if relevant; tag with the class name if the question is class-based; approximate the level of the question.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Try to avoid creating new tags — check for existing synonyms or popular tags first. When choosing between two equally appropriate tags, choose the more populated one. If you must create a new tag: use all lowercase, don't use symbols, and replace spaces with dashes. Related links explain tagging conventions in more detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Why was my question voted down?
rubrics_metrics.description: Common reasons: the question may be inappropriately phrased, belong on another forum, be unclear (especially to non-native English speakers), or simply be not understandable to readers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To reduce downvotes, make the question more specific, include examples or diagrams if helpful, explain context, and include formulas that clarify the issue. Note: explanations for downvotes are not required, and occasional accidental downvotes happen.

rubrics_metrics.name: Why was my 'What is [X]?' question downvoted or closed?
rubrics_metrics.description: If your 'What is X?' question was downvoted or closed, check the comments for specific feedback and edit your question to address the issues noted.
